title: メディア情報専門実験・演習B
subtitle: Media Informatics Major Lab/Exercises B
educationalGoal: This course is separated into following two parts. The “PC Assembly and Network” part aims to foster the knowledge and skills needed to build a personal computer from parts and construct a simple network. In the "Physical Computing" part, students are required to create an original system consisting of I/O devices connected to a microcomputer and learn about practical interaction designing.
advice: "PC Assembly and Network" In this part of the course, the following experiments and exercises will be conducted: assembly of a standard desktop PC, configuration of the BIOS, installation of an operating system, assembly of the LAN cable, building and configuring Ethernet networks, connecting to local networks using a HUB, building servers, and troubleshooting. “Physical Computing” The goal of this part of the course is to realize a human-oriented interaction through experiments designed to create many kinds of interactions using I/O devices connected to a microcomputer. Students are required to participate actively in the class and engage in teamwork. Safety must be observed at all times. Compliance with scheduled actions and careful treatment of the equipment and tools are also required. All items must be restored to their original conditions when the class is over. Copyright infringement related to class work is strictly prohibited. To pass this course, students grade points must exceed 60% for each part. If any point is less than 60%, the student will fail the entire course.
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have fundamental knowledge about PCs, networks, and programming. Since safety is a top priority, students must follow instructions from supervisors and work carefully during the exercises.

activityGoals.body: Be able to assemble and configure a properly functioning PC based on correct knowledge and handling of the parts
Be able to construct a simple LAN using multiple PCs and hubs.
Be able to give a presentation about your work.
Be able to connect and control a microcomputer and input/output devices.
Be able to create and produce original interaction designs.
